JPL 10/18/26 John Wesley Part 2 - Will You Let God Work Through You?
Show Opening Slide for Series
Show slide of John Wesley.
1) A Person Must Realize They are Lost Before they are Saved.
“Then one of the criminals who were hanged blasphemed Him, saying, “If You are the Christ, save
Yourself and us.” But the other, answering, rebuked him, saying, “Do you not even fear God,
seeing you are under the same condemnation? And we indeed justly, for we receive the due
reward of our deeds; but this Man has done nothing wrong.” Then he said to Jesus, “Lord,
remember me when You come into Your kingdom.” And Jesus said to him, “Assuredly, I say to
you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.””
Luke 23:39-43 NKJV
"The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God."
(Romans 8:16)
2) You Must Be Born Again and Set On Fire
“And He said to them, “Why did you seek Me? Did you not know that I must be about My Father’s
business?””
Luke 2:49 NKJV
"Faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone." — James 2:17, KJV
3) A Disciplined Faith Must Become a Living Faith
John Wesley said, "I look upon all the world as my parish."
"Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be
filled." (Luke 14:23)
4) Identify Your Go
5) Faith Must Have Hands and Feet
"I was an hungry, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger,
and ye took me in." (Matthew 25:35)
"Faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone." (James 2:17)
Societal transformation would be achieved from the inside out, one individual at a time, each
person undergoing a personal reformation.
How is it with your soul?
6) We Grow Better Together
"Let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the
assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another."
(Hebrews 10:24-25)
7) One Surrendered Life Can Influence Generations
God's kingdom has always advanced through ordinary acts of faithfulness.
Do not confuse visibility with significance.
But you can be faithful where God has placed you.
Your assignment is not to become another John Wesley. Your assignment is to be faithful to
Jesus Christ with the life He has given you.
What are you doing with your influence?
Who are you encouraging?
Who are you teaching?
Who are you serving?
Who is learning what it means to follow Jesus by watching your life?
Conclusion: There is a Great Work to be Done - Will You Let
God Work Through You?
The most important question is what God wants to accomplish through us.
"Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable
service." — Romans 12:1, KJV
God is not asking every person to become a famous preacher. He is calling every believer to
surrender.
Whatever your circumstances, you can offer your life to God.
The question is whether you will make that offering.
Will you allow Him to transform your heart?
Will you follow Him when obedience costs you something?
Will you serve people who cannot repay you?
Will you invest in the next generation?
Will you continue growing in His love?
May our lives, like Wesley's, point people towards the Savior who alone is worthy of our
devotion.
